PLAHIS Planning Application Reference: DM2024/01755--- Address: Sutton Business ParkRestmor WayHackbridgeSM6 7AH--- Proposal: Erection of a two-storey building comprising six flexible / mixed use (Use Class B2, B8, EG(iii)) business units along with the delivery of soft landscaping / planting and delivery of enhanced biodiversity measures--- Status: REC--- Decision: --- Date Decision Issued: ---

description: Erection of a two storey detached building comprising 6 self contained mixed use industrial units (Use Class ((B2/B8 and EGiii)), ancillary office space at mezzanine level with vehicle parking and cycle spaces, sub station and boundary treatment.
decision_conditions: Occupier
The development must be begun not later than the expiration of three years beginning with the date hereof.Reason: To comply with Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990, as amended.

Prior to commencement of groundworks (excluding site investigations anddemolition), a final detailed surface water drainage strategy shall be submitted to andapproved by the Local Planning Authority. This should demonstrate that infiltration hasbeen maximised by proposed SuDS including the attenuation system. A final drainagelayout should be provided to show the location and specifications (gradients, pipe sizes,invert levels, and storage volumes of SuDS features) of the proposed drainage system tothe point of discharge. The drainage layout should demonstrate that the required bufferdistance requirements between the base of infiltration systems and a building has beenmet. Pipe gradients must be revised to align with Building Regulations, H3.15, BritishStandard 752-2008, and CIRIA SuDS Manual guidance.Reason: To ensure the development is made safe without increasing flood risk elsewherein accordance with the National Planning Policy Framework (Planning and flood risk) andassociated guidance, policy SI13 of the London Plan 2021, policy 32 of the Sutton LocalPlan 2018, and the National standards for sustainable drainage systems.

Prior to the first occupation of any of the commercial units hereby approved, adetailed Parking Management Plan for the site shall be submitted to and approved inwriting by the Local Planning Authority. The Plan shall specify, but not be limited to:1. The designation and operational management of all on-site parking spaces, includingthe 36 car parking spaces, disabled persons' parking bays, and electric vehiclecharging points.2. The means by which the parking associated with the adjacent commercial units willcontinue to be managed and relocated to ensure no net loss in parking or overspillonto the local highway network.3. The methods of enforcement and monitoring to ensure the car parking provision isused and retained exclusively for its designated purpose.The approved Parking Management Plan shall be implemented prior to the firstoccupation of the development and shall be adhered to and retained for the lifetime of thedevelopment.Reason: To ensure the parking provision is appropriately managed, does not result in aloss of existing parking, and to comply with Policy 37 of the Sutton Local Plan.

Prior to commencement of the development (excluding demolition), a BiodiversityGain Plan and an associated Habitat Management and Monitoring Plan must besubmitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority (LPA). TheBiodiversity Gain Plan shall:1. Demonstrate how the development will achieve a minimum 10% net gain;2. Include details of on-site habitat creation, enhancement and management measures,including the type, extent and condition of each habitat;3. Provide a timetable for implementation and completion.The accompanying Habitat Management and Monitoring Plan shall:1. Set out management objectives, prescriptions and responsibilities;2. Specify monitoring methodology;3. Cover a minimum of 30 years from completion of habitat creation works.The development shall thereafter be carried out in accordance with the approvedBiodiversity Gain Plan and Habitat Management and Monitoring Plan.Reason: To secure the Biodiversity Net Gain in accordance with the Environment Act2021 and Policy 34 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

Prior to the first occupation of any of the commercial units hereby approved, adetailed Servicing and Delivery Plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by theLocal Planning Authority. The Plan shall set out how all deliveries and servicingoperations will be managed and shall include, but not be limited to:1. Full details of the designated on-site loading and unloading areas, access, andegress routes for all service and delivery vehicles.2. Measures to ensure that all vehicles can be accommodated within the site and do notqueue or wait on the public highway.3. Specific measures to manage the servicing and deliveries, such as noise mitigationmeasures and ways to prevent increased road traffic.4. Details of any consolidation of deliveries and the promotion of low or zero-emissionvehicles where feasible.5. The process for waste management, storage, transfer, and collection on site.6. A clear process for long-term review and update of the plan to reflect operationalchanges.The approved Servicing and Delivery Plan shall be implemented prior to the firstoccupation of the development and shall be adhered to and retained for the lifetime of thedevelopment.Reason: To ensure that the delivery and servicing of the site does not cause congestion,inconvenience, or safety issues on the local highway network, and to promote sustainabletransport measures in accordance with Policies 29 and 36 of the Sutton Local Plan.

The development hereby approved shall be constructed in accordance withthe approved Energy Statement (Revision 004) prepared by ESC and dated 11 November2024 together with the approved air source heat pump (ASHP) and solar PV details. Priorto first occupation of the development, 'as-built' Standard Assessment Procedure (SAP)outputs must be submitted to the Local Planning Authority and approved in writing todemonstrate that the development has achieved the targetedreduction in CO2 emissions. All of the approved measures must thereafter be retained foras long as the development is in existence.Reason: To comply with Policy 31 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018

Prior to first occupation, documentary evidence including finalised dynamic thermalmodelling results must be submitted to the Local Planning Authority and approved inwriting which demonstrates that the overheating strategy has been implemented in linewith the approved details.Reason: To comply with London Plan Policy SI 4.

Within 12 weeks of the commencement of development, a BREEAM NewConstruction V6.1 Design Stage Certificate, issued by the Building ResearchEstablishment (BRE) or equivalent authorizing body, must be submitted to the LocalPlanning Authority and approved in writing to show that an 'Excellent' rating will beachieved and that the score targeted in the pre-assessment has been met or exceeded.Reason: To comply with Local Plan Policy 31.

Within 12 weeks of the occupation of the development, a BREEAM NewConstruction V6.1 Post-Construction Certificate, issued by the BRE or equivalentauthorizing body, must be submitted to the Local Planning Authority and approved inwriting to demonstrate that an 'Excellent' rating has been achieved in accordance with theapproved details. All the measures integrated shall be retained for as long as thedevelopment is in existence.Reason: To comply with Local Plan Policy 31.

Prior to occupation of the development the car parking shall be laid out inaccordance with drawing no. 4144_PL103N and shall be retained thereafter for thelifetime of the development.Reason: To comply with policy 37 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

Prior to the first occupation of each individual commercial unit, a detailed Waste andRefuse Management Strategy specific to that unit shall be submitted to and approved inwriting by the Local Planning Authority. The approved Strategy shall be implemented andadhered to for the lifetime of the respective unit's use.Reason: To ensure adequate provision is made for the storage and removal of waste andto protect amenity in accordance with policy 28 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

Prior to the first occupation of any commercial unit, a detailed Access Managementand Security Strategy for the pedestrian and cycle link to New Mill Quarter shall besubmitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Strategy shallinclude details of the hours of operation, physical security measures, CCTV, and lighting,and shall be implemented prior to first use of the link and permanently retained.Reason: To ensure the link operates safely and securely while promoting sustainabletransport in accordance with policies 28, 29 and 36 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

No building hereby permitted shall be occupied until evidence (e.g. photographs andinstallation contract) demonstrating that the sustainable drainage scheme for the site hasbeen completed in accordance with the approved details has been submitted to andapproved by the Local Planning Authority. A detailed management plan confirming whatmanagement company shall be responsible for the routine maintenance tasks for alldrainage components must also be submitted. The sustainable drainage scheme shall bemanaged and maintained thereafter in accordance with the agreed management andmaintenance plan for all of the proposed drainage components.Reason: To ensure the development is made safe without increasing flood risk elsewherein accordance with the National Planning Policy Framework (Planning and flood risk) andassociated guidance, policy SI13 of the London Plan 2021, policy 32 of the Sutton LocalPlan 2018, and the National standards for sustainable drainage systems.

Prior to the first occupation of the development, the noise mitigation measuresdetailed in the Noise Impact Assessment (Report Reference: 250710, Revision 2, dated10/07/25) shall be fully implemented and retained thereafter. This shall include, but not belimited to, the walls and roof being constructed using the Euroclad Elite 55 system (oracoustically equivalent, minimum 41 dB Rw, and the rear external exit doors achieving aminimum sound reduction rating of 29 dB Rw.Reason: To safeguard the amenity of the nearest residential receptors, in accordance withPolicy 29 of the Sutton Local Plan.

The development must be carried out in accordance with the provisions of theapproved Fire Statement by EMCO Final v1 issued 30/10/2024.Reason: To ensure that the development incorporates the necessary fire safety measuresin accordance with the Mayor's London Plan Policy D12.

The site and building works required to implement the development shall be onlycarried out between the hours of 08.00 and 18.00 Mondays to Fridays and between 08.00and 13.00 on Saturdays and not at all on Bank Holidays and Sundays.Reason: To safeguard the amenity of surrounding occupiers in line with Policy 29 of theSutton Local Plan.

If during implementation of this development, contamination is encountered whichhas not previously been identified, the additional contamination shall be fully assessedand a specific contaminated land assessment and associated remedial strategy shall besubmitted to and agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority before the additionalremediation works are carried out. The agreed strategy shall be implemented in full priorto the completion of the development hereby approved.Reason:To prevent harm to human health and pollution of the environment in accordancewith the aims and objectives of Policy 34 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

All Non-Road Mobile Machinery (NRMM) of net power of 37kW and up to andincluding 560kW used during the course of the demolition, site preparation andconstruction phases shall comply with the emission standards set out in chapter 7 of theGLAs supplementary planning guidance Control of Dust and Emissions DuringConstruction and Demolition dated July 2014 (SPG), or subsequent guidance. Unless itcomplies with the standards set out in the SPG, no NRMM shall be on site, at any time,whether in use or not, without the prior written consent of the local planning authority. Thedeveloper shall keep an up to date list of all NRMM used during the demolition, sitepreparation and construction phases of the development on the online register athttps://nrmm.london/.Reason: To comply with Policy 34 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

No deliveries to or from the site in connection with the construction of thedevelopment shall take place outside the hours of 09:30 to 15:00 Monday to Friday. Nodeliveries shall take place on Saturdays, Sundays or Bank/Public Holidays.Reason: To avoid conflict with peak traffic periods, minimise disruption to the localhighway network and safeguard residential amenity in accordance with policies 29 and 36of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

Prior to the commencement of development (excluding demolition) the type andtreatment of the materials, including samples, to be used on the exterior of the building(s)shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Theapproved materials shall be used in the construction of the development herebyapproved, completed prior to its occupation/use and permanently retained thereafter.Reason: To safeguard the visual amenities of the area and to ensure compliance withpolicy 28 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

Prior to the commencement of the development (excluding demolition works), fulldetails of the secure cycle storage facilities shall be submitted to, and approved in writingby, the Local Planning Authority which shall show their positioning within the site, the sizeand materials of the enclosure and the means of access. The approved details shall beimplemented on site prior to the first occupation of the development hereby approved andthereafter permanently retained in accordance with the approved details.Reason: To ensure the development provides an adequate level of cycle parking facilitiesand to encourage sustainable modes of transport, in accordance with policies 36 and 37of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

Prior to the occupation of the development, full details of hard and soft landscapingshall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. All hard andsoft landscaping and tree planting shall be carried out in accordance with the approveddetails and to a reasonable standard in accordance with the relevant recommendations ofappropriate British Standards (in particular, BS 3882: Specifications for Topsoil,Recommendations (2015) and BS 8545: Trees from Nursery to Independence in theLandscape, Recommendations (2014) or other recognised codes of good practice). Theworks shall be carried out prior to the occupation of any part or relevant phase of thedevelopment or in accordance with the timetable agreed with the Local PlanningAuthority. Any tree(s) or plants that (within a period of five years after planting) areremoved, die, or (in the opinion of the Local Planning Authority) are damaged or defectiveshall be replaced as soon as is reasonably practicable with others of a similarsize/species/number as originally approved, unless the Local Planning Authority gives itsconsent to any variation.Reason: To ensure the provision, establishment and maintenance of a reasonablestandard of landscape in accordance with the approved designs in accordance with Policy28 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

Prior to first occupation of development, detailed proposals for postimplementationmonitoring and reporting on energy performance over a period of five years must besubmitted to the Local Planning Authority and approved in writing. The proposals mustaccord with step 4 'Be Seen' of the Mayor's energy hierarchy; the GLA's Be Seen EnergyMonitoring Guidance (2021) and CIBSE TM54 methodology.Reason: To comply with London Plan Policy SI 3.

Prior to first occupation of development, an Overheating Assessment must besubmitted to the Local Planning Authority and approved in writing which sets out details ofproposed cooling and ventilation measures and demonstrates that the proposeddevelopment complies with CIBSE TM52 Guidance.Reason: To comply with London Plan Policy SI 4.

Prior to the commencement of development, an updated ESC BREEAM Tracker mustbe submitted to the Local Planning Authority and approved in writing includingconfirmation that a BREEAM 'Excellent' rating is targeted and an outline of the latestprogress towards meeting or exceeding the scores targeted at the BREEAMpreassessment stage.Reason: To comply with Local Plan Policy 31.

Prior to the commencement of development, documentary evidence must besubmitted to the Local Planning Authority and approved in writing to show that thedevelopment will achieve an improved Green Space Factor (GSF) score compared to thebaseline GSF score for the site prior to redevelopment. The council's GSF scoring systemset out in the council's 'Technical Guidance Note - Building a Sustainable Sutton' (June2018) must be used for this purpose. The development shall be carried out in accordancewith the approved details and thereafter retained.Reason: To comply with Policy 33 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

Prior to the commencement of works at the site a Dust Management Plan must besubmitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The DMP mustinclude monitoring of dust deposition, dust flux, real-time PM10 continuous monitoringand/or visual inspections. This plan must incorporate the recommendations of (Table 9:Mitigation Measures to be Incorporated into the DMP/ CEMP for the ProposedDevelopment) of the Air Quality Assessment and be in compliance with the GLA Controlof Dust and Emissions during Construction and Demolition SPG.Reason: To comply with Policy SI1 of the London Plan 2021 and Policy 34 of the SuttonLocal Plan 2018
